claim: In the general (non-orbifold) collapsing-manifold class, the stability theorem (Theorem 1.5) gives only an abstract continuous increasing modulus of continuity omega(s) with omega(0)=0, and no explicit rate or exponent is derived for it.
stance_target: the finding that general spectral-geometric stability results are qualitative, not quantitative
scope_conditions: class MMp(n,Lambda,D) of pointed complete Riemannian manifolds with bounded diameter and sectional curvature, and their measured Gromov-Hausdorff closure
quoted_support: there exists an increasing, continuous function ω(s) = ω(r,n,Λ,D)(s) that depends on r, n, Λ, D, which maps ω : [0, 1) →[0, ∞) with ω(0) = 0, such that ... dpmGH((X, p, µ), (X′, p′, µ′)) < ω(δ).

claim: An explicit modulus of continuity becomes available only in the special case where the limit space is a priori a Riemannian orbifold (dim X = n-1), stated as Theorem 1.6 in Part I but proved in Part II.
stance_target: quantitative stability is exclusively achievable in the orbifold specialization of this inverse problem
scope_conditions: X a Riemannian orbifold in class MMp(n,Lambda,D,Lambda3), interior spectral data on a ball in the regular part
quoted_support: If (X, p, µ) ∈MMp(n, Λ, D) is a priori an orbifold, i.e., dim(X) = n−1, it is possible to obtain an explicit form of the modulus of continuity ω, given the interior spectral data {λj, ϕj|BX(p,r)} for the weighted Laplacian ∆X on a ball BX(p, r) ⊂Xreg, provided that the metric tensor on the regular part Xreg is of class C4.

claim: Theorem 1.5's stability estimate removes the injectivity-radius assumption present in an earlier stability result for this class of manifolds, applicable when X, X' are themselves n-dimensional manifolds (non-collapsed case).
stance_target: prior stability results this paper improves on
scope_conditions: n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with bounded diameter and sectional curvature
quoted_support: In particular, in the case of the spaces X, X′ being n-dimensional manifolds, Theorem 1.5 removes the injectivity radius assumption for the stability result in [3].
